projects.title: Obstacle-Avoiding Robot
projects.objective: Build a mobile robot that drives forward and turns away from walls on its own.
steps: 1. Assemble the chassis and mount the motors.
2. Wire the motors to the L298N driver (Motor A and Motor B).
3. Connect the L298N control pins to the microcontroller.
4. Mount the HC-SR04 sensor on the front of the chassis.
5. Connect Trig and Echo to digital pins.
6. Write and upload the obstacle-avoidance code.
7. Test on a flat surface with obstacles.
8. Tune the threshold and turn duration.
projects.expected_behavior: Robot drives forward and turns when it gets within 20 cm of an obstacle.
troubleshooting: Robot spins in place: threshold too high or sensor reading stuck.
Motors don't move: check L298N power jumpers and ENA/ENB PWM.
Erratic readings: mount sensor away from motors.
Robot turns wrong way: swap motor polarity or change turn direction.
extension_challenges: Add a left-turn fallback for corners.
Add a second ultrasonic sensor for wider coverage.
Log distance readings to Serial Monitor for analysis.

projects.title: Automatic Night Lamp
projects.objective: Build a lamp that turns on automatically when it gets dark.
steps: 1. Build a voltage divider with the LDR and 10 kO resistor.
2. Connect the divider output to an analog pin (A0).
3. Connect the LED to a digital pin through a 220 O resistor.
4. Write code to read the light level and control the LED.
5. Test in bright and dark conditions.
6. Adjust the threshold for your environment.
projects.expected_behavior: LED turns on in darkness and off in bright light.
troubleshooting: LED never turns on: check resistor and LED polarity.
Always on or always off: adjust the threshold value.
Flickering: add delay or average multiple readings.
extension_challenges: Fade the LED smoothly using PWM.
Add a buzzer that beeps when light changes.
Log light readings to Serial Monitor.
